question: The Government of the Autonomous Community of Catalonia (Catalan Government) has used Next Generation funds to cut Spanish out of Catalan education. The Sánchez Government, a prisoner of its own associates, has done nothing to stop it.

Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan funding to the tune of EUR 200 million has been allocated to the Catalan Digital Education Plan to distribute robotics kits, audiovisual equipment and laptops with software exclusively in Catalan across 2 827 schools, in line with the Estratègia d’impuls digital drawn up by Catalonia’s Department of Education.

In addition, EUR 900 000 has been used to buy books for Catalan public libraries. The requirement that 50 % of the books in each library be in Spanish has not been fulfilled. La Asamblea por una Escuela Bilingüe (a bilingual schooling association) has condemned the fact that only 19 % of children’s books, 36 % of young adult books and 49 % of books for adults purchased were in Spanish.
In light of this fraudulent use of funds: 1.
What is the Commission going to do about EU funds being used to violate the right and obligation to use Spanish as Spain’s, and of course Catalonia’s, official language?
The European Parliament is investigating whether or not the political desire to cut Spanish out of Catalan education is harmful to students. Does the Commission believe this is the case?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.4.2024) 1. The implementation of Spain’s Recovery and Resilience Plan is framed by the Council Implementing Decision (CID)1.

It includes milestone 289 providing for ‘connected digital devices […] in public and publicly subsidised schools, in cooperation with the Autonomous Communities’, which was deemed satisfactorily fulfilled by the Commission during the second payment request. Target 291 includes the ‘provision of connected and interactive digital devices for at least 300 000 students and equipment for at least 240 000 classrooms’.

The deadline for this target is 31 December 2025, during the ninth payment request. Based on the CID, the language settings of the provided devices are not part of the Commission’s assessment. Member States must ensure that projects supported by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) comply with EU and national law, as per the RRF Regulation2. 2.

Article 165 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union provides that the EU must fully respect Member States’ responsibility for teaching content and education system organisation, including cultural and linguistic diversity. Decisions on bilingual education, including those on language of curriculum and number of hours of instruction in a certain language, fall within the Member States’ domain.
The European objective in language learning3 is that children finish secondary education mastering two other languages in addition to the language of schooling.
